edges.mechanism: Mg2+ forms insoluble chelates with tetracyclines (doxycycline, demeclocycline), reducing antibiotic absorption. Take antibiotic >=2 h before or 4-6 h after magnesium.
edges.evidence: NIH ODS; PK crossover: Al/Mg antacid cut doxycycline AUC from 38.6 to 6.0 mg.h/L (subtherapeutic)

edges.mechanism: Chelation reduces fluoroquinolone (ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin) absorption. Interaction strongest when Mg is given within 4 h before the dose.
edges.evidence: NIH ODS; PK crossover: ciprofloxacin relative bioavailability 15%, 23%, 70% with antacid 5-10 min, 2 h, 4 h before; none at 6 h before or 2 h after

edges.mechanism: Magnesium-rich supplements or antacids decrease absorption of oral bisphosphonates (e.g. alendronate). Separate by >=2 h.
edges.evidence: NIH ODS fact sheet recommendation

edges.mechanism: Divalent cation complexation lowers levothyroxine absorption. Mg aspartate reduced T4 AUC 12%, Mg citrate 7% (NS). Separate dosing.
edges.evidence: Randomized crossover PK trial in 15 healthy adults (ThyroMag)

edges.mechanism: Magnesium oxide reduces intestinal absorption of gabapentin. Cmax down 33%, AUC down 43%, bioavailability down 32%.
edges.evidence: Randomized crossover PK study, n=13

edges.mechanism: Long-term PPI use (typically >1 year) causes hypomagnesemia, sometimes refractory to supplementation (25% of FDA-reviewed cases needed PPI withdrawal). FDA advises baseline and periodic serum Mg.
edges.evidence: MA of 16 observational studies: adjusted OR 1.71 (1.33-2.19), high dose OR 2.13; FDA/ODS; case reports

edges.mechanism: Thiazides increase urinary Mg loss. Associated with hypomagnesemia (OR 2.74-3.14), mainly with >390 days of use. Not seen when combined with a potassium-sparing agent.
edges.evidence: Rotterdam Study cross-sectional, n=9820; NIH ODS

edges.mechanism: Loop diuretics increase urinary Mg excretion and can cause depletion with chronic use. Not linked to hypomagnesemia in a population cohort.
edges.evidence: NIH ODS; Rotterdam Study

edges.mechanism: Amiloride/spironolactone reduce Mg excretion. Additive retention is possible with high-dose Mg, especially with reduced renal function.
edges.evidence: NIH ODS; mechanism only for accumulation

edges.mechanism: Calcineurin inhibitors are a common drug cause of renal Mg wasting and hypomagnesemia, e.g. in kidney transplant recipients.
edges.evidence: Narrative reviews

edges.mechanism: SGLT2 inhibitors raise serum Mg and are proposed as a treatment for hypomagnesemia. Consider when dosing Mg in CKD.
edges.evidence: Narrative reviews

edges.mechanism: Metformin is associated with hypomagnesemia (GI losses, TRPM6 suppression). Mg supplementation slightly lowers FBG/HbA1c, a small additive glycemic effect.
edges.evidence: Case plus narrative review; MA of 78 RCTs (FBG -3.60 mg/dL, HbA1c -0.15%)

edges.mechanism: Additive BP lowering. Larger SBP reduction (-7.68 mmHg) in hypertensive people on BP-lowering medication.
edges.evidence: MA of 38 RCTs (subgroup); high heterogeneity

edges.mechanism: Magnesium added to fluoxetine gave greater HDRS reduction (-6.35 vs -2.80).
edges.evidence: Small non-blinded randomized trial (n=40); low certainty

edges.mechanism: Reduced renal clearance leads to accumulation and hypermagnesemia (hypotension, arrhythmia, cardiac arrest). eGFR <=55 and BUN >=22 independently predicted hypermagnesemia on MgO. MAGiCAL-CKD saw more GI AEs and numerically more deaths/CV events on Mg.
edges.evidence: NIH ODS; retrospective cohort n=320; case series; RCT n=148

edges.mechanism: Retained Mg laxative acts as an absorption reservoir. Fatal hypermagnesemia reported even with normal renal function, and in older adults with constipation and renal dysfunction.
edges.evidence: Case reports/series

edges.mechanism: Hidden additional Mg (e.g. 500 mg elemental per tablespoon of milk of magnesia). Very large doses (>5000 mg/day) cause toxicity. Counts toward the 350 mg/day supplemental UL.
edges.evidence: NIH ODS; case reports

edges.mechanism: Very high supplemental zinc (142 mg/day) decreased Mg absorption and Mg balance.
edges.evidence: Metabolic balance studies in adult men; NIH ODS

edges.mechanism: Shared divalent cation handling. In a stable-isotope crossover study, raising calcium from 800 to 1800 mg/day did not significantly alter Mg absorption, kinetics or balance.
edges.evidence: Small stable-isotope study (n=5 adolescent girls); low certainty

edges.mechanism: Vitamin D hydroxylases are Mg-dependent. Mg supplementation modulates 25(OH)D depending on baseline (raises near 30 ng/mL, lowers at 30-50 ng/mL). Mg glycinate plus D3 raised 25(OH)D more than D3 alone.
edges.evidence: Two RCTs (n=180, n=95)

edges.mechanism: Hemolysis falsely raises measured Mg. Serum Mg (<1% of body Mg, homeostatically defended) is a poor marker of status. Normal values do not exclude depletion, and oral repletion may not change serum Mg.
edges.evidence: Experimental hemolysis study; NIH ODS; reviews; RCT showing urinary but not serum rise
